refinedPositionCandidate.elevationNote: Camera elevation kept at the printed/catalog 1570 m (5151 ft). 3DEP 1 m ground at this point is 1572.1 m; this is a local summit.
refinedPositionCandidate.assumption: The camera 'Delilah Lookout 2' is mounted on, or at the summit of, the Delilah fire lookout. Not stated by any source consulted; supported only by the elevation match (printed 5151 ft = 1570 m vs 3DEP 1572.1 m at the lookout point) and by the name.

demHorizonCheck.source: OpenTopoData ned10m (USGS NED 1/3 arc-sec, bilinear), 1 deg azimuth x 500 m rays 1-40 km from the refined position, k=0.13 refraction, camera z=1570
demHorizonCheck.finding: Terrain skyline from azimuth 0-110 deg stays between +1.5 and +3.3 deg elevation with no sharp unique feature; it cannot pin down yaw or tilt by eye. Printed Y (+7.33) cannot be a geometric tilt-up: the visible ridge would then sit at or below y~217 and the frame ridge is at y~193-250 with the upper ridge at the right edge near y~195.

refinedPositionCandidate.elevationNote: Kept catalog 2578 m. Printed 8468 ft = 2581.0 m. 3DEP summit near (-118.8608, 36.7370) = 2582.9 m. Buck Rock lookout summit is quoted at 8,502 ft (2591 m) by news and the Forest Service, so the camera would sit ~10 m under that figure.
refinedPositionCandidate.assumption: The camera is on the Buck Rock lookout summit. Supported by: the database coordinate and an independent DEM summit search agreeing within ~25 m, and the elevation match. No source states camera mounting.

hypothesesNotForFitting.identificationMethod: Visual reading of the dark pointed foreground peak in the lower left, matched to the DEM skyline local maximum at azimuth ~273-275 deg, 7.5 km (-1.85 deg elevation). Visual only.
hypothesesNotForFitting.whyNotUsable: With the printed Z 1.4 and catalog FOV 65.1 deg at zoom 1, the rising massif at the right edge would sit ~1.5-3 deg higher than this peak, but the image shows ~4.9 deg (48 px). Printed zoom is not verified to map to FOV. Treat as unresolved; do not feed to calibration.py.

demHorizonCheck.source: OpenTopoData ned10m, azimuth 255-345 deg, 1-40 km, k=0.13
demHorizonCheck.finding: Skyline rises smoothly from about -3 deg (azimuth 255) to +0.3 deg (azimuth 345). The near ridge at 7-8.5 km (azimuth 255-295) sits at -1.8 to -3.0 deg.

catalogMetadataLeads.meaning: The 65.1 deg field is the catalog horizontal FOV at zoom 1 (unverified). az_current is the live pan at the snapshot time, not the Garnet frame pose. Its datum (true vs magnetic vs relative) is not documented. How printed X maps to az_current is NOT established.
catalogMetadataLeads.suggestedTest: Read the printed X/Y/Z of one current frame of each camera and compare with az_current/tilt_current at the same timestamp. Two poses per camera would give offset and scale. Not done here (it would mean downloading live imagery; left to the coordinator).

overlayAxes.finding: X cannot be used as true azimuth. Using the origin bearing as a stand-in gives incompatible offsets between cameras, and the fire is not at the origin on 2025-08-27 anyway. Y does not behave as a geometric tilt (see demHorizonCheck). Z may be zoom; unverified.

limitations: Both refined positions are candidates, not surveyed antenna positions.
No reference pairs were verified; the CAL FIRE origin point was not used for fitting or validation.
DEM heights are bare earth (3DEP/NED), datum NAD83/NAVD88; no geoid or WGS84 conversion applied. Tower height above ground unknown.
calibration.py assumes camera at the given origin with no position fit; a 300-500 m position error is large against a 10-20 km baseline.
